title: The stoning
hook: pebbles thrown at pillars where Ibrahim rejected Shaytan's whispers

segments.voice: Yesterday, the night at Muzdalifah, and your line: a night under the sky. Did you look up before you slept, even for a minute? Day one thousand one hundred thirty-three.

Small stones. That's what the morning after Muzdalifah comes down to. On the day of sacrifice, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ reaches a pillar in the valley at Mina and throws pebbles at it, one at a time. Before that, on the road, he asks Ibn Abbas to pick some up for him. Ibn Abbas brings back little ones, the kind you could flick between a finger and a thumb. The Prophet shakes them in his hand and says: like these. Not rocks. Not anything bigger to make a point. Today's word is the place those small stones are thrown.
screen: `SMALL STONES.` → `PICK SOME UP FOR ME.` → `LIKE THESE.`

segments.voice: Jamarat. The pillars of Mina, and the rite of stoning them. Start with what the Prophet did. In Jabir's account in Sahih Muslim, he comes to the jamrah, throws seven small pebbles, and says Allahu akbar with each one. A throw, and God is greater. A throw, and God is greater. Next, the size, and a warning. In the report from Ibn Abbas in al-Nasa'i, after the Prophet says like these, he adds a caution: beware of going to extremes in religion, because extremes destroyed those who came before. The pebbles are small on purpose. The rite doesn't need anger to work. Then, the story people tell. A report attributed to Ibn Abbas says that at these spots Shaytan appeared to Ibrahim, trying to turn him from what God had asked, and Ibrahim drove him off with stones. It isn't in the Qur'an. It's a report kept in the hadith books, and the tradition remembers the stoning through it. Last, what the rite is for. Aisha is reported, in Sunan Abi Dawud, to have said that the circling of the House, the walk between Safa and Marwa, and the stoning were set up for the remembrance of God. So the target isn't really the pillar. The Qur'an's closing surah names the enemy: "the sneaking whisperer, Who whispereth in the hearts of mankind." A whisper is quiet. It doesn't shout. It suggests. And the answer the rite rehearses is just as quiet: a small stone, a clear refusal, God is greater. Pilgrims do it again in the days that follow. A whisper comes back, so the refusal comes back too.
screen: `SEVEN PEBBLES, A TAKBIR EACH.` · `SMALL, ON PURPOSE.` · `IBRAHIM DROVE HIM OFF.` · `SET UP FOR REMEMBRANCE.` · then, large: `THE SNEAKING WHISPERER.`

segments.voice: The practice: reject one whisper. Settle, and breathe. Let one familiar thought come up, the quiet one that nudges you toward something you'd rather not do. Putting off the call. The sharp reply. The extra hour of scrolling. Don't fight it. Just name it, plainly, as a whisper. If you pray, you can say a'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ir-rajim, the words Muslims use to seek refuge from Shaytan. If you don't, picture a small stone in your hand, and set the thought down with it. Then breathe again. The bell holds the time.
Jamarat. The pillars at Mina where pilgrims throw small pebbles, a takbir with each, remembering Ibrahim's refusal. Today's word.
Your line: reject the whisper. Today, when that quiet nudge comes back, say no once, small and clear, without making a scene of it. Tomorrow: the sacrifice. Day one thousand one hundred thirty-three.

howItsDone: On the day of sacrifice pilgrims throw small pebbles at the pillar called Jamrat al-Aqabah at Mina, saying Allahu akbar with each, and on the following days they stone all the pillars.

notes: Muslim 1218 (Jabir): seven pebbles at the jamrah on the day of sacrifice, takbir with each, pebbles like those used for flicking. Confirm.
Nasa'i 3057 (Ibn Abbas): 'pick up for me', small pebbles, 'like these', and the warning against extremes in religion. Confirm number and grading.

The Ibrahim-and-Shaytan story is attributed to Ibn Abbas (al-Hakim, al-Bayhaqi, Ibn Khuzaymah); presented as a report the tradition keeps, not as Qur'an. Confirm the citation and whether a Keeper wants a grading note.
Abu Dawud 1888 (Aisha): stoning and sa'y established for the remembrance of Allah. Confirm number and grading (some grade it weak).
Pickthall 114:4–5 wording ('From the evil of the sneaking whisperer, Who whispereth in the hearts of mankind'): verify exactly before release.
'Pilgrims do it again in the days that follow' anticipates the days of tashriq (day 1137); kept brief.
The isti'adhah formula is a real, widely used phrase (cf. 16:98), offered 'if you pray'; no new prayer written.

Editor: 'weighs them' changed to 'shakes them' to follow Nasa'i's report; Aisha's Abu Dawud report now names all three rites it lists (tawaf, sa'y, stoning); howItsDone names Jamrat al-Aqabah instead of the unsourced 'largest pillar'.
